result:
There is a specific, profound magic hidden in the concept of "liminal spaces"—those fleeting, transitional moments that exist in the soft borders between what was and what will be. We usually rush through them, entirely unaware of their quiet gravity. Think of the hushed, metallic hum of an airport terminal at three in the morning, the eerie, muffled stillness of a snow-covered street just before dawn, or the ethereal, fading amber light of a late November afternoon. 

These in-between places and moments temporarily suspend reality. They areThresholds where the relentless, crushing weight of yesterday finally lifts, yet the anxious, buzzing demands of tomorrow have not fully materialized. In these fragile pauses, we are completely unbound. 

I find incredible peace in the quiet rebellion of simply pausing to acknowledge these spaces. Instead of hurrying through the transition to reach a planned destination, what if we chose to exist purely within the transition itself? There is a subtle kind of liberation in realizing you belong to no one in these moments. You are neither the person you were nor the person you are about to become. You are merely a consciousness drifting through the architecture of time.

We spend our lives urgently seeking meaningful destinations, convinced that purpose is found only at the summit or the end of the long road. But there is a brilliant, untamed beauty in the journey across the threshold. It is a gentle reminder that we are always, in some sense, simply becoming.
